subject: AI & Agents
title: Who Controls the Foundation Models?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Who Controls the Foundation Models?.

hook.text: Five companies control the most powerful AI models on Earth. That's a lot of power for a few hands.

buildup.text: Training frontier models costs hundreds of millions, limiting who can compete.

discovery.text: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, and a few others set the capabilities and limits of AI.

twist.text: Their safety decisions, content policies, and access rules shape what billions of people can do.

climax.text: Open-source models redistribute power, but frontier capabilities remain concentrated.

punchline.text: Whoever builds the model writes the rules.

quiz.question: Why is AI power concentrated in few companies?
options: Training frontier models costs hundreds of millions of dollars
Only a few people understand AI

details.summary: A handful of tech companies control the most powerful AI foundation models. This concentration of power raises concerns about who sets the rules for AI that billions of people rely on daily.
details.whyItMatters: Foundation model makers shape what AI can and cannot do for the entire ecosystem. Democratic governance of this power is essential to prevent corporate overreach.
takeaways: A few companies control the most powerful AI foundation models
These models underpin thousands of downstream applications
Concentrated power demands democratic oversight mechanisms

faq.question: Which companies control the major foundation models?
faq.answer: OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Meta, and a few others dominate. Their models underpin chatbots, coding tools, image generators, and countless other applications worldwide.

faq.question: Why is foundation model concentration a problem?
faq.answer: A few companies set safety policies, content filters, and capability limits for AI used by billions. Without competition and oversight, their priorities may not align with public interest.
